significance: Marks the Sun's entry into Capricorn and the start of Uttarayan, the Sun's northward journey. A harvest festival and an especially auspicious time for charity and holy dips.
how_celebrated: Early holy dip, Surya arghya, daan of til, jaggery, khichdi and warm clothes, family feasts and kite flying.
traditional_foods: til-gud laddu, khichdi, gajak, pheeni, ghevar
muhurat_rule: Punya Kaal / Maha Punya Kaal after the Sankranti moment is best for snan and daan.
regional_notes: Jaipur and Rajasthan: huge kite-flying (patangbazi) day, called Sakraat; daan and feasts of ghevar/pheeni. Punjab: Maghi. Gujarat: Uttarayan. Tamil Nadu: Pongal.

significance: Punjabi winter-harvest festival celebrating the passing of the longest nights and the new crop.
how_celebrated: Evening bonfire with songs and dancing; popcorn, peanuts, revri and gajak are offered to the fire.
traditional_foods: revri, gajak, popcorn, peanuts, sarson da saag
regional_notes: Mainly Punjab, Haryana, Delhi and North India.

tithi: Thai Pongal (first day of Tamil month Thai)
significance: Tamil harvest festival thanking the Sun, nature and cattle.
how_celebrated: Rice is boiled with milk in a new pot until it overflows; kolam designs, sugarcane, and cattle worship (Mattu Pongal).
regional_notes: Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Tamil diaspora.

significance: Welcomes spring and honours Goddess Saraswati, the goddess of knowledge, music and arts.
how_celebrated: People wear yellow, worship Saraswati with books and instruments, and children are introduced to writing (Vidyarambh).
muhurat_rule: Purvahna (forenoon) puja when Panchami is present.
regional_notes: Rajasthan and North India: yellow clothes and yellow food; Bengal: Saraswati Puja in schools; Punjab: kite flying.

significance: The great night of Shiva, commemorating Shiva-Parvati's marriage and Shiva's cosmic dance. Devotees stay awake and fast.
how_celebrated: Night-long jagran, abhishek of the Shivling with water, milk, curd, honey and ghee, offering bel patra, chanting Om Namah Shivaya; four-prahar puja.
muhurat_rule: Nishita Kaal (midnight) puja; four prahar puja through the night.
regional_notes: Jaipur and Rajasthan: abhishek at Shiv temples and long queues; Ujjain Mahakaleshwar; Varanasi Kashi Vishwanath.

significance: Commemorates the victory of devotion (Prahlad) over evil (Holika). The bonfire burns negativity.
how_celebrated: Community pyre is lit after puja with raw thread, grain ears, coconut and water; people circle the fire and take its ash.
muhurat_rule: After sunset during Pradosh Kaal on Purnima; avoid Bhadra Kaal.
regional_notes: Rajasthan/Haryana: badkule (cow-dung garlands) offered to the fire; Gujarat and Maharashtra also big.

significance: Festival of colours celebrating spring, love and the triumph of good over evil.
how_celebrated: Playing with dry colours (gulal) and water, music, dance, meeting family and neighbours, special sweets.
traditional_foods: gujiya, thandai, malpua, dahi bhalla, mathri
regional_notes: Brij (Mathura, Vrindavan, Barsana: Lathmar Holi), Rajasthan (colourful and rural phag songs), West Bengal (Dol Jatra).

significance: Worship of Sheetla Mata, protector from pox and heat-related illnesses, especially for children's health.
how_celebrated: Food is cooked the previous evening and eaten cold (basi bhojan); Sheetla Mata is offered the cold food with water and roli.
traditional_foods: rabri, dahi, roti, pua, cold kheer
muhurat_rule: Morning puja, no fresh cooking that day.
regional_notes: Big in Rajasthan (Sheetla Mata mela near Chaksu, Jaipur), Gujarat, UP and Haryana.

significance: Rajasthan's women-centred festival honouring Gauri (Parvati) and Isar (Shiva) for marital happiness and good husbands.
how_celebrated: Girls and women make and decorate clay idols, sing Gangaur songs, apply mehendi and fast; ends with a procession and visarjan.
muhurat_rule: Final-day puja on Chaitra Shukla Tritiya, evening procession.
regional_notes: Jaipur's royal Gangaur procession from the City Palace area; also Jodhpur, Udaipur, Bikaner; observed in Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat too.

name_hi: हिंदू नववर्ष / विक्रम संवत् / उगादी / गुड़ी पड़वा
name_en: Hindu New Year (Vikram Samvat / Ugadi / Gudi Padwa)
significance: Chaitra Shukla Pratipada begins the lunar year (Vikram Samvat) and Chaitra Navratri; also Ugadi, Gudi Padwa and Cheti Chand in different regions.
how_celebrated: Panchang puja, neem-jaggery eaten, rangoli, flags (gudi) and home cleaning.
regional_notes: Maharashtra: Gudi Padwa; Karnataka/Telangana/AP: Ugadi; Sindhi: Cheti Chand; North India: Chaitra Navratri begins.

significance: Nine days of Shakti worship in spring, ending with Ram Navami.
how_celebrated: Ghatasthapana, nine days of fasting and Durga path, Ashtami/Navami kanya pujan and havan.
traditional_foods: kuttu, singhara atta, sabudana, fruits, halwa-puri-chana
regional_notes: Strongest in North and West India; Rajasthan: devotees visit local Devi temples and fairs.

significance: Birth of Lord Rama, the seventh avatar of Vishnu, ideal of dharma.
how_celebrated: Midday birth puja (Ram Janma), Ramcharitmanas path, bhajans, processions and Ram darbar decoration.
muhurat_rule: Madhyahna (midday) is the Ram Janma moment.
regional_notes: Ayodhya's large celebrations; Rajasthan: Ram temples and Ram Navami shobha yatra.

significance: Birth anniversary of Mahavira, the 24th Jain Tirthankara, teaching ahimsa, truth and non-possession.
how_celebrated: Abhishek of Mahavira idols, rath yatra, charity, temple visits and sermons.
traditional_foods: sattvic food, no root vegetables for many families
regional_notes: Major in Rajasthan, Gujarat and Maharashtra Jain communities (Jaipur has a large Jain population).

significance: Birth anniversary of Hanuman, symbol of strength, devotion and service.
how_celebrated: Sunrise puja with sindoor chola, Hanuman Chalisa and Sundarkand path, offering laddu/boondi, bhandara.
regional_notes: Rajasthan: Mehandipur Balaji and Salasar Hanuman temples draw huge crowds; Tamil/Kerala/AP date differs.

significance: One of the most auspicious days of the year: anything started or given in charity is believed to bring lasting (akshaya) merit.
how_celebrated: Puja of Vishnu and Lakshmi, daan, buying gold or silver, starting new ventures; Jains mark Varshi Tap parana.
regional_notes: Rajasthan: Akha Teej is also an agricultural new-season day when farmers start work and read omens.

significance: Celebrates the birth, enlightenment and nirvana of Gautama Buddha.
how_celebrated: Monastery and temple visits, meditation, charity, release of caged animals, readings of Buddhist texts.
regional_notes: Bodh Gaya, Sarnath, Lumbini (Nepal), Sikkim and Ladakh.

significance: Marks the descent of Ganga to earth; holy dip is said to cleanse sins.
how_celebrated: Early dip in Ganga or any river, Ganga aarti, daan of water vessels and sherbet.
regional_notes: Haridwar, Varanasi, Prayagraj and along the Ganga; also in Rajasthan at ponds and rivers.

significance: The strictest Ekadashi; fasting without water on this day is believed to equal observing all 24 Ekadashis.
how_celebrated: Vishnu puja, no food or water until next sunrise, daan of water pots, fans and sherbet.
muhurat_rule: Parana the next morning in the Dwadashi window.
regional_notes: Widely observed in North India; sherbet stalls (chhabeel) are common.

significance: Married women fast for their husband's long life, inspired by Savitri who won back Satyavan's life from Yama.
how_celebrated: Women worship the banyan tree, tie raw thread around it, circle it 7 or 108 times and read the Savitri-Satyavan katha.
muhurat_rule: Morning puja under the banyan tree.
regional_notes: North India observes it on Jyeshtha Amavasya; Maharashtra/Gujarat on Jyeshtha Purnima (Vat Purnima).

significance: Annual chariot journey of Lord Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra from the Puri temple to Gundicha temple.
how_celebrated: Huge wooden chariots are pulled by devotees; bhajans and prasad distribution.
regional_notes: Puri (Odisha) main; ISKCON and Jagannath temples hold smaller yatras across India including Jaipur.

significance: Honours teachers and gurus; the day commemorates Vyasa, compiler of the Vedas and the Mahabharata.
how_celebrated: Pada puja of gurus, offering flowers and dakshina, satsang, reading scriptures; many also take a holy dip.
regional_notes: Observed by Hindus, Buddhists and Jains alike; Govardhan parikrama (Mathura) is popular.

significance: Monsoon festival celebrating the reunion of Shiva and Parvati; women pray for marital happiness.
how_celebrated: Green clothes and bangles, mehendi, swings (jhula) decorated with flowers, folk songs and Teej Mata puja.
muhurat_rule: Morning to evening puja with Teej katha.
regional_notes: Jaipur's Teej procession carrying Teej Mata is famous; in Rajasthan Teej and Gangaur are the major women's festivals.

significance: Worship of serpent deities; thanks and protection from snakes.
how_celebrated: Milk, haldi and flowers offered to snake images; no digging or cutting of the earth that day.
regional_notes: Maharashtra (Battis Shirala), Rajasthan (Nag temples) and South India.

deity: भाई-बहन का पर्व (इंद्राणी-इंद्र, कृष्ण-द्रौपदी की कथा)
significance: Celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters; sisters tie a rakhi and brothers promise protection.
how_celebrated: Sister performs aarti, applies tilak, ties rakhi, offers sweets; brother gives a gift.
muhurat_rule: Rakhi to be tied outside Bhadra Kaal, usually in the afternoon.
regional_notes: Rajasthan: sisters also tie 'Lumba' rakhi to bhabhis; Maharashtra Narali Purnima; Gujarat Pavitropana.

significance: Birth of Lord Krishna at midnight in Mathura.
how_celebrated: Midnight abhishek of Laddu Gopal, jhula, bhajans, jhankis; next day Dahi Handi in Maharashtra.
regional_notes: Mathura-Vrindavan, Dwarka and Jaipur's Govind Dev Ji temple draw big crowds; Maharashtra: Dahi Handi.

significance: Women observe a strict fast commemorating Parvati's penance to win Shiva.
how_celebrated: Sand or clay idols of Shiva-Parvati, night jagran, offering bel patra and shringar items to Parvati.
muhurat_rule: Pradosh or Pratahkala puja on Tritiya.
regional_notes: UP, Bihar, Nepal, Maharashtra, Rajasthan.

significance: Birth of Lord Ganesha, remover of obstacles; prayers begin new ventures.
how_celebrated: Ganesha idol installed (pranpratishtha), daily aarti with modak and durva, immersion on a chosen day or Anant Chaturdashi.
muhurat_rule: Madhyahna Ganesh puja Muhurat on Chaturthi (avoid moon sighting on this night per tradition).
regional_notes: Maharashtra (Mumbai, Pune) is the biggest; Jaipur's Moti Doongri Ganesh Temple has special celebrations; Wednesdays are Ganesh days.

significance: Vishnu Ananta puja and the final day of Ganesh immersion.
how_celebrated: Anant sutra (14-knot thread) tied after puja; Ganesh idols immersed with processions.
muhurat_rule: Morning puja, visarjan in the afternoon/evening.
regional_notes: Mumbai's Lalbaugcha Raja immersion; observed in Rajasthan with Ananta vrata.

significance: Honours Vishwakarma, divine architect; workers, artisans and engineers worship their tools and machinery.
how_celebrated: Factory and workshop cleaning, tool worship, food distribution.
regional_notes: West Bengal, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Assam and industrial belts.

significance: Sixteen-day period to honour ancestors through tarpan, pind daan and shraddh.
how_celebrated: Shraddh on the tithi of the ancestor's death, tarpan with water and black sesame, feeding Brahmins and offering to cows, crows and dogs, charity.
muhurat_rule: Kutup Kaal / Rohina Kaal (midday) is the best time for shraddh.
regional_notes: Gaya (Bihar), Pushkar, Haridwar, Prayagraj are key pind daan places; Sarva Pitru Amavasya for unknown tithi.

significance: Nine nights honouring the nine forms of Durga, culminating in Dussehra.
how_celebrated: Ghatasthapana on day 1, daily worship of each form, fasting, Garba and Dandiya in Gujarat, Durga Puja in Bengal, Ashtami/Navami kanya pujan.
traditional_foods: kuttu atta dishes, sabudana, fruits, singhara
muhurat_rule: Ghatasthapana in the first third of the day or Abhijit Muhurat.
regional_notes: Garba-dandiya (Gujarat), Durga Puja pandals (Bengal), Ramlila (North), Bathukamma (Telangana); Rajasthan: Mata temples and fairs.

significance: The final two days of Navratri; Sandhi Puja, kanya pujan and havan are performed.
how_celebrated: Kanya pujan (feeding nine girls), Durga havan, Ayudha/shastra pujan on Navami.
muhurat_rule: Sandhi Kaal puja at the Ashtami-Navami junction; havan by Pradosh.
regional_notes: Bengal's Sandhi Puja; Kota/Jaipur: havan in temples.

significance: Victory of good over evil: Rama's win over Ravana and Durga's win over Mahishasura.
how_celebrated: Ravana effigy burning, shastra and Shami pujan, Aparajita puja, Ramlila culmination.
muhurat_rule: Aparahna (afternoon) puja; effigy burning at dusk.
regional_notes: Kota Dussehra Mela is famous in Rajasthan; Mysuru Dasara, Kullu Dussehra, Delhi Ramlila.

significance: Brightest moon of the year; believed to shower nectar-like rays. Lakshmi is said to bless those awake (Kojagari).
how_celebrated: Kheer kept under moonlight and eaten as prasad; Lakshmi and Kojagara puja; Raas Leela in Vrindavan.
regional_notes: Gujarat: Garba; Bengal: Kojagari Lakshmi Puja; North India: kheer in moonlight.

deity: भगवान शिव, माँ पार्वती, गणेश, चंद्र
significance: Married women fast for their husbands' longevity and well-being, breaking the fast after sighting the moon.
how_celebrated: Sargi before dawn, nirjala fast, solah shringar, group katha in the evening, arghya to the moon through a sieve, husband gives first sip.
muhurat_rule: Evening puja Muhurat and moonrise time (city specific).
regional_notes: Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, UP, Delhi and MP; moonrise time differs by city.

significance: Mothers fast for children's well-being; Ahoi Mata is worshipped at dusk.
how_celebrated: Ahoi Mata drawn or hung on the wall, evening katha, arghya to stars (or moon) to break the fast.
regional_notes: North India (UP, Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana).

significance: First day of Diwali; Dhanvantari, the physician of the gods, emerged with the nectar pot. Buying metals or utensils is auspicious.
how_celebrated: Puja of Dhanvantari, Lakshmi and Kuber at Pradosh; buying gold, silver, utensils; Yamadeep Daan (a lamp for Yama) in the evening.
regional_notes: Jaipur's jewellery and Johari Bazaar markets are packed; many buy brooms and kitchenware.

significance: Krishna's victory over the demon Narakasura; Abhyang Snan (oil bath) before sunrise is said to remove sins.
how_celebrated: Abhyang snan with ubtan and til oil before sunrise, evening diyas, worship of Yama and Hanuman (Kali Chaudas).
muhurat_rule: Abhyang snan during the Chandrodaya-Sunrise window.
regional_notes: Roop Chaudas in Rajasthan/Gujarat; Kali Chaudas in Gujarat and Bengal (Kali puja at night).

significance: Festival of lights marking Rama's return to Ayodhya and the worship of Lakshmi, goddess of wealth.
how_celebrated: Home cleaning and rangoli, lighting diyas, Lakshmi-Ganesh puja at Pradosh, chopda pujan in shops, sweets exchange, fireworks.
traditional_foods: laddu, kaju katli, gujiya, mathri, khil-batasha
muhurat_rule: Pradosh Kaal with Sthir Lagna (Vrishabha) is best; Nishita Kaal for Tantric puja.
regional_notes: Jaipur markets (Bapu Bazaar, Johari Bazaar) are lit up for Diwali; Gujarati New Year follows; Bengal: Kali Puja.

significance: Krishna lifted Govardhan hill to shelter Vrindavan from Indra's rain; Annakut offers a mountain of food.
how_celebrated: Cow-dung Govardhan figure circled and worshipped, Annakut (56 bhog) offered, cows decorated.
traditional_foods: annakut, kadhi, bajre ki roti, sweets
regional_notes: Mathura-Vrindavan, Nathdwara (Rajasthan), Jaipur Govind Dev Ji temple; Gujarati New Year (Bestu Varas).

significance: Sisters pray for brothers' long life; Yama visited his sister Yamuna on this day.
how_celebrated: Tilak on the brother's forehead, aarti, sweets; brother gives gifts.
regional_notes: Bhau Beej (Maharashtra), Bhai Phonta (Bengal).

significance: Four-day Sun worship from Bihar, UP and Jharkhand for family well-being.
how_celebrated: Nahay-Khay, Kharna, Sandhya Arghya at sunset, Usha Arghya at sunrise at river or pond banks with bamboo soop offerings.
muhurat_rule: Exact sunset and sunrise times of your city.
regional_notes: Bihar, Jharkhand, eastern UP, Delhi and diaspora.

significance: Vishnu wakes after four months of sleep (Chaturmas); weddings and auspicious work resume.
how_celebrated: Fast, Vishnu puja, sugarcane mandap in the courtyard, chants of 'Uthho Dev' and Tulsi Vivah preparations.
regional_notes: North India, Maharashtra (Kartiki Ekadashi, Pandharpur).

significance: Ceremonial marriage of Tulsi with Shaligram (Vishnu) marking the start of wedding season.
how_celebrated: Tulsi decorated as a bride with chunri and shringar, mandap of sugarcane, pheras with Shaligram, aarti.
regional_notes: Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra and UP.

significance: Holy full moon of Kartik: Ganga snan, deepdan and Shiva's victory over Tripurasura.
how_celebrated: Holy dip, deepdan with thousands of diyas on ghats, Satyanarayan katha.
regional_notes: Varanasi's Dev Deepawali, Pushkar Fair and holy dip in Rajasthan, Guru Nanak Jayanti.

significance: Birth anniversary of the first Sikh Guru, Guru Nanak Dev Ji.
how_celebrated: Akhand Path, nagar kirtan processions, langar and gurdwara decoration.
regional_notes: Punjab, Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan; Nankana Sahib (Pakistan).

significance: Birth of Kalabhairava, the fierce form of Shiva, protector of time and travelers.
how_celebrated: Night puja, mustard-oil lamp, offering black sesame and urad, feeding dogs, Bhairav Chalisa.
regional_notes: Ujjain Kal Bhairav temple, Varanasi Kal Bhairav.

deity: भगवान श्री राम और माता सीता
significance: Marriage anniversary of Rama and Sita, celebrated especially in Ayodhya, Janakpur and Mithila.
how_celebrated: Ram-Sita vivah rituals, Ramcharitmanas path, bhajans.
regional_notes: Janakpur (Nepal), Ayodhya; many avoid wedding on this day in Mithila.

significance: The day Krishna taught the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna on the Kurukshetra battlefield; coincides with Mokshada Ekadashi.
how_celebrated: Gita path, discourses, Vishnu puja, fast.
regional_notes: Kurukshetra celebrates with an international Gita Mahotsav.

significance: Kerala's harvest festival welcoming King Mahabali.
how_celebrated: Pookalam floral carpets, Onasadya feast, boat races, Kathakali, Pulikali.
regional_notes: Kerala and Malayali diaspora.

significance: The eleventh tithi of each fortnight is dedicated to Vishnu; fasting without grains is believed to cleanse mind and body.
how_celebrated: Fast, Vishnu and Tulsi puja, Vishnu Sahasranama, parana next morning.
muhurat_rule: Parana in the Dwadashi window next morning.
regional_notes: Observed by Vaishnavas across India; 24 per year (26 in an Adhik Maas year).

significance: Full-moon day observed with Satyanarayan katha, moon worship and holy dips.
how_celebrated: Fast, Satyanarayan katha with panchamrit and sooji halwa prasad, moon arghya.
regional_notes: Widely observed in Gujarat, Rajasthan, UP and Maharashtra.

significance: New-moon day dedicated to ancestors (tarpan), Shani, and spiritual practices.
how_celebrated: Pitru tarpan, daan, holy dips, Shani puja on Saturdays.
regional_notes: Somvati and Mauni Amavasya are particularly significant.

significance: Shiva worshipped at twilight on Trayodashi of both pakshas.
how_celebrated: Fast, evening abhishek, bel patra, Shiva aarti.
regional_notes: Somvar Pradosh and Shani Pradosh are special.

significance: Monthly Chaturthi fast for Ganesha, broken after moonrise.
how_celebrated: Fast, Ganesh puja with durva and modak, moon arghya.
regional_notes: Angarki Chaturthi (Tuesday) is the most auspicious.
